title: Stream synchronization failure: token-stitching protocol and capacity fallback plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-02-26 led to elevated client disconnects and truncated/partial tokens for a subset of streaming responses during a bursty traffic window. Root cause analysis found two contributing issues: (1) an incompatibility between the tokenizer version used by the frontend gateway and the serving runtime that caused token boundary disagreement during reassembly, and (2) an aggressive backpressure heuristic that dropped in-flight fragments when GPU pool queues spiked, which prevented graceful continuation of streams. The combination produced clients receiving partial tokens and failing to reconnect cleanly. This ticket captures the mitigation plan, persistent fixes, and observability additions required to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-26 02:13 UTC: First alerts — elevated stream error rates and increase in client reconnects in us-west
2026-02-26 02:25 UTC: Oncall throttled traffic and flipped to secondary routing policy to reduce load on primary GPU pool
2026-02-26 03:10 UTC: Initial mitigation — temporarily relaxed backpressure eviction threshold to allow fragment buffering
2026-02-26 08:00 UTC: Incident commander declared Sev2; post-incident RCA kicked off
2026-02-27 14:00 UTC: Tokenizer mismatch discovered between edge gateway (v3.1) and runtime (v3.0) during replay tests
2026-03-01 09:30 UTC: Engineering triage created ENG-48123 and assigned owners for three workstreams
action_items: Standardize tokenizer versioning: introduce runtime + gateway compatibility headers and fail-fast if versions diverge (owner: Aisha) — implement by 2026-03-14

Implement token-stitching protocol: server will emit explicit token-boundary markers in the stream and a lightweight resume token to allow clients to request continuation without duplicating content (owner: Backend Streaming Team) — RFC and prototype by 2026-03-21

Backpressure harmonization: replace current drop-on-surge heuristic with a two-stage policy: buffered soft-throttle + prioritized tail-replay queue for in-flight fragments (owner: Runtime Performance) — rollout window runtime-1.20
KV-cache version checks: add per-session KV cache epoch headers and runtime assertions to detect and log mismatches early (owner: Cache Team) — include in metrics and alerts
End-to-end harness: add synthetic test that replays high-concurrency streaming sessions with interleaved version toggles to CI (owner: QA) — target in-cycle coverage

Capacity fallback automation: extend smart routing to divert new streams to warm spare pools after sustained queue latency above SLO for 30s (owner: Orchestration) — add dashboard and incident automation

Observability: create a streaming continuity dashboard that surfaces 'partial-token' rate, average fragment reassembly time, and tokenizer-version skew by region (owner: Observability) — dashboard and alerting by 2026-03-18
Runbook update: update streaming-runbook with token-stitching play, backpressure mitigation steps, and a checklist for safe rollback of runtime heuristics (owner: SRE)
acceptance_criteria: No tokenizer-version skew incidents for 72 hours in canary region after deployment
Partial-token rate < 0.01% of streaming responses in production for 7 consecutive days post-release
Automated E2E test reproduces previous symptom locally and shows the new stitch/resume path succeeds in >95% of trials
Dashboard emits an alert when fragment reassembly rate degrades or when backpressure eviction events exceed threshold
risks_and_mitigations: Rolling new token-boundary markers may break older SDKs: mitigate by shipping backward-compatible embedding (marker optional) and by advertising capability via version header
Buffered soft-throttle increases memory pressure during long spikes: mitigate with per-session caps and prioritized tail-replay eviction
Routing to spare pools could expose customers to higher-cost variants: mitigate by tagging diverted traffic and applying soft quota controls and customer-facing communication
notes: PM requested customer comms template for impacted tiers (work item added to PM backlog)
Design to consult on SDK resume UX to avoid duplicate-token rendering in popular web players
Consider a short-lived compatibility flag on the gateway to force v3.0 tokenization for impacted customers during migration
